boundary: This ledger uses public evidence proxies for category leadership and landing-page maturity. It does not claim private conversion-rate proof.

tightNiche.job: Growth and marketing teams need to see competitor, market, search, social, and AI-visibility changes early enough to act.
tightNiche.pageJob: Make Five to Nine feel like a credible market-intelligence SaaS landing page, not a generic AI redesign.

notes: ARR, revenue, customer count, acquisition value, and funding are stronger performance proxies than visual similarity.
Mobbin search relevance alone is not performance proof.
If Mobbin lacks an exact leader, the replacement must be labeled visualProxy.

publicEvidence.claim: Over 6,500 customers, including 88% of the S&P 100.

factsVsInference.inference: Enterprise market-intelligence north star for credibility, IA, proof density, and high-stakes decision language.

leaderboard.category: online visibility, SEO, GEO, competitive research

publicEvidence.claim: Adobe completed the Semrush acquisition on April 28, 2026, strengthening brand visibility capabilities.

factsVsInference.inference: Best-fit public benchmark for search, AI visibility, competitive research, and buyer-safe SaaS proof.

leaderboard.category: social listening and customer signal intelligence
leaderboard.proxyType: official revenue and enterprise customer count

publicEvidence.claim: Sprout reported 3,803 customers contributing at least $30K ARR and 2,022 contributing at least $50K ARR.

factsVsInference.inference: Strong visual and structural model for social/consumer-signal monitoring and enterprise CTA discipline.

leaderboard.category: digital market intelligence and competitive traffic analysis

publicEvidence.claim: 6,128 customers and 454 customers with $100K+ ARR as of December 31, 2025.

factsVsInference.inference: Direct benchmark for market-traffic proof, competitor trend framing, and data credibility.

leaderboard.category: search, competitor, backlink, and AI visibility data

publicEvidence.claim: Ahrefs reports 400M monthly AI prompts, 35T live backlinks, 19.2B content pages, and 217 locations covered.
Ahrefs Site Explorer positions competitor growth, traffic, keywords, backlinks, paid ads, and Brand Radar as core workflows.

leaderboard.confidence: high for product scale, medium for revenue

factsVsInference.inference: Useful benchmark for data-scale storytelling, but revenue/conversion performance is not public here.

leaderboard.category: media, social, AI, and competitive intelligence
leaderboard.proxyType: official customer count and platform breadth

publicEvidence.claim: Meltwater combines media, social, and AI signals into one intelligence platform.

leaderboard.confidence: high for customer count, medium for revenue

factsVsInference.inference: Useful benchmark for multi-signal positioning and broad intelligence architecture.

More than 2,000 marketers from over 500 organizations rely on the platform daily.

leaderboard.confidence: high for traction, medium for revenue

factsVsInference.inference: Strong emerging-category reference for AI-search visibility and product-screenshot proof.

leaderboard.category: AI search analytics and brand visibility

publicEvidence.claim: Raised $21M Series A to help brands win in AI search.
Peec reports 1,300+ brands and agencies onboarded since February 2025, 300+ customers added per month, and $4M+ ARR in 10 months.

factsVsInference.inference: Most visually direct Mobbin reference for Five to Nine's AI/search visibility side, but still an emerging challenger.

publicEvidence.claim: Trusted by half of the Forbes 100.

factsVsInference.inference: Useful category benchmark, but less direct to 0509 than Sprout/Meltwater.

publicEvidence.claim: Klue says 250,000+ users rely on the platform and that it ranks as a G2 industry leader in 4 categories.

factsVsInference.inference: Strong category-fit proof, but weaker public scale data than the top eight.

publicEvidence.claim: Crayon remains a direct category reference for competitive intelligence; use as category-fit proof, not revenue proof.

factsVsInference.inference: Useful for feature vocabulary and buyer job, but not enough public performance evidence for the top eight.

requiredDesignConsequence: The visual direction must feel like a serious SaaS intelligence product: clear enterprise nav, one very strong headline, visible product artifact, source/status proof, category-specific metrics, and buyer-safe CTA. It must not reuse the earlier generic Mobbin Proving Lab public-home flavor.
